knowledge_gaps: The residual is a reasonable experiment, but its originality is modest. Difficulty 3 understates sparse graph construction, full-catalog scoring, serialization, and diagnostic adaptation.

Reproduction requires exact transition counting, diagonal removal, normalization/pruning order, neighborhood size, recency window, decay, score-scale estimator, zero-variance handling, and blend grid. Top-K storage alone does not bound co-occurrence construction cost.

The diagnostic interface needs a concrete way to retain history prefixes alongside neural features: combined residual scores cannot generally be recovered from SASRec feature vectors alone. Each training-position diagnostic must use its causal prefix. Graph edges containing the diagnosed training target can inflate margins, so those margins cannot establish generalization.

No baseline validation scores, branch coverage, or complementary-error measurements establish that the residual deserves priority over a loss change. Searching many blend settings on 200 validation users per category risks selection overfitting.
Transitions and co-occurrence may amplify popularity or broad associations. The proposed connection to compatibility and satisfied needs remains unverified, as the report acknowledges.

follow_up_queries.reason: Find a reproducible, scalable graph recipe and clarify how much novelty the residual offers over established item-neighborhood methods.
follow_up_queries.query: For sequential recommendation combining SASRec with sparse item-item residual scores, how do ItemKNN, session-based kNN, and transition-count baselines construct binary-user cosine similarities and directed transitions? Compare diagonal removal, normalization before versus after top-K pruning, popularity correction, and blockwise sparse construction that avoids materializing a dense item-item matrix.

follow_up_queries.reason: Resolve the missing diagnostic implementation and prevent training-target associations from being mistaken for evidence of improved next-item generalization.
follow_up_queries.query: How should a hybrid Transformer and training-history item-transition recommender compute causal per-position positive-negative diagnostics? Explain carrying sequence prefixes alongside hidden features, contamination when graph statistics include the diagnosed target interaction, and leave-one-user-out graph diagnostics versus ordinary in-sample diagnostics.

follow_up_queries.reason: Specify a small, informative experiment and limit validation selection bias before spending the shared GPU budget.
follow_up_queries.query: For a SASRec plus transition/co-occurrence score ensemble evaluated with 200 fixed validation users per dataset and 99 sampled negatives, what methods assess complementary ranking errors and validation hyperparameter selection bias? Include paired user bootstrap uncertainty for four-dataset macro HR@10, branch coverage and popularity ablations, candidate-independent score calibration, and comparison with gSASRec generalized BCE.
